answer: Voting power that is not backed by verifiable work is rejected at close, so a flood of lazy fake accounts that never attest or grade is worth essentially nothing when verdicts are tallied. The key insight is that coordination itself leaks: the more unified a farm is, the more easily its shared style or timing betrays it. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale. Consider a summit as the anchor of the cost.
